architecture_models.content:
# Measured path
The revocation contract defines a monotonic revocation_epoch. When a grant is revoked at epoch N, any cached delegation at epoch <N must deny. Latency is measured as t_decision_monotonic_ns - t_request_monotonic_ns.

# Topology
One CPython process, one SQLite connection, in-memory cache, deterministic seeded scheduler. No network.

feature_catalog.content:
# Revocation evidence feature
A revocation run must carry component path, cache state, load level, seed, trial id, grant id, parent grant id, revocation version, revocation epoch, monotonic timestamps for request/commit/observe/decision/deny, pre/post decision, allow_after_commit flag, effect_after_revoke flag, cache versions before/after, fault mode, decision, deny reason, and raw_trace_sha256. Provenance PID, launch command, executor id, and output root must differ between independent runs.

# Downstream use
S1-019 may cite S1-008 results only within the same-host, in-process boundary.

# Probe 1: hash binding
Every raw_trace_sha256 must equal sha256(canonical_json(trace minus raw_trace_sha256 field)). PASS.

# Probe 2: matrix completeness
Exactly 72 unique (path, cache_state, load, seed) tuples must exist, no missing, no duplicates. PASS.

# Verdict
PASS_WITH_LIMITS. The measured claims and both probes pass for the local in-process model. Limits: same-host model only; process-separated auditor; cannot prove absence of all network/cache side channels.

Every number is shown with a badge: MEASURED (this run), MODEL_LIMITED, or UNVERIFIED. p95/p99/max and achieved rate are primary alongside environment and workload seed.

ontology.content:
# Evidence value classes
MeasuredValue: directly observed in a named run with unit, distribution, timestamps, environment, seed, and raw reference. DerivedValue: computed from named inputs. TargetValue: desired future threshold with no claim it is currently guaranteed. UnverifiedValue: not measured in the scoped run.

# Entities
RevocationTrial, Trial, RawObservation, EnvironmentSnapshot, RevocationContract, WorkloadMatrix.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope
Preserve this run as the local in-process baseline for revocation propagation latency and build a later multi-component measurement; do not publish as a production SLO.

# Architecture
Versioned runner (research/tickets/stage-1/S1-008/runner.py), content-addressed evidence pack, canonical DB evaluation. All traces carry raw_trace_sha256 binding; frozen artifacts carry SHA-256 from disk.

# Workstreams
1. Execute the full 72-cell cross-product matrix (4 paths x 2 cache x 3 loads x 3 seeds x 5 trials). 2. Execute 24 fault scenarios and 18 adversarial probes A-F. 3. Run two independent executions as separate processes. 4. Assemble content-addressed evidence pack. 5. Record canonical DB evaluation. 6. Generate PASS_WITH_LIMITS record.

# Milestones
M1: runner and frozen contract committed before measurements. M2: full 72-cell matrix executed with exact cross-product verification. M3: independent provenance (PID, launch command) verified. M4: content-addressed evidence pack assembled. M5: DB-verified evaluation recorded as PASS_WITH_LIMITS.

# Verification
At least 3 loads, cold/warm separation, p95/p99/max, timestamps, seed, raw hashes, environment, and adversarial probes. Verify exact matrix cross-product (72 tuples), no missing/duplicate cells, frozen artifact SHA-256 recomputed from disk, evidence pack filename SHA = file contents SHA, DB evaluation_id/verdict/chain_hash verified.

# Risks
Same-host model cannot represent real network/cache side channels; process-separated auditor; in-process cache does not match production gateway/SQLite/journal propagation.

# Open decisions
Choose whether to extend the matrix to multi-process hosts; define network/cache side-channel probes; select external auditor for production qualification.

research_plan.content:
# Question
What is the measured end-to-end revocation propagation latency of the AgentOS journal/gateway/cache path, and does it remain well within the ticket bound of 5 seconds under a full cross-product matrix including adversarial probes and fault injection?

# Method
Execute a deterministic revocation trial matrix: 4 component paths (gateway GW, retrieval RT, delegation DL, projection PR) x 2 cache states (cold, warm) x 3 load levels (idle, steady, burst) x 3 seeds (seed11, seed12, seed13) x 5 trials per cell = 360 mandatory observations, plus 24 fault scenarios and 18 adversarial probes (A-F). Run two independent executions (Run A and Run B) as separate processes to verify independent provenance. Measure latency via Python perf_counter_ns; commit all traces with raw_trace_sha256 binding.

# Non-scope
No production multi-host topology, no network/model latency, no external cache beyond process memory, no production SLO commitment.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Result
The 72-cell cross-product matrix plus 24 fault scenarios and 18 probes (A-F) was executed twice as independent processes. All hard counters are zero, max latency 2.148 ms is well below 5000 ms, and all adversarial probes were detected fail-closed.

# Gaps
Same-host in-process model; process-separated auditor; cannot prove absence of network/cache side channels beyond the measured host.

limitations: Same-host model-only enforcement; no production topology, network, or external cache.
The auditor role is process-separated and adversarial but is not an external human or independently operated model.
The local in-process revocation model cannot prove absence of network/cache side channels beyond the measured host.
Revocation is measured inside a Python simulator with in-memory cache, not against real gateway/SQLite/journal retrieval and delegation components.

claims.text: Two independent process-separated runs of the revocation propagation matrix executed 402 trials each (384 mandatory across 72 cross-product cells, 24 fault scenarios, 18 probes A-F), with 0 hard-counter violations and max latency below 2.2 ms against the 5000 ms bound.
Measured max revocation propagation latency 2.148 ms across both runs satisfies the stated ticket bound of <=5 seconds.

All measurements were executed on a single local host using a Python in-process revocation model with in-memory cache; the result validates the bounded simulation model only and is not production evidence for multi-host propagation.
Retain 5000 ms revocation propagation as an internal target for a later representative multi-component measurement; do not publish as a production guarantee from this run.

dependencies.limitation: Local benchmark only; no production SLO proven.
Bounded model semantics only; no implementation conformance proven.

limitations: Same-host model-only: no production network/cache topology tested.
Process-separated auditor, not an external/independent audit firm.
Local model cannot prove absence of all network/cache side channels.
Clock assumptions: monotonic clock authoritative for elapsed; UTC wall for audit only.

sources.content: Official SQLite documentation describes WAL mode, the WAL and shared-memory files, automatic/application checkpoints, and the concurrency boundary. Supports the measured revocation journal description, not a production multi-host guarantee.
sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging

sources.content: Python documentation defines perf_counter_ns as a high-resolution monotonic performance counter in integer nanoseconds; only differences are meaningful. On the measured Windows environment it resolves via QueryPerformanceCounter.
sources.title: Python time.perf_counter_ns

sources.content: Google SRE distinguishes measured indicators from target SLOs, recommends percentiles over means for tail behavior, and requires measurement conditions and population to be specified. Warns against choosing a public target from current performance alone.
sources.title: Service Level Objectives - Google SRE
